classification.difficultyReason: Link routine intercept calculations, cube-root rearrangement, translated inflection points and coefficient signs to construct consistent cubic sketches.

content.prompt:
Draw a neat sketch of these equations.
Clearly label the $y$-intercept, $x$-intercept.

answer.worked:
When $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=(0-2)^3+7\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
Let $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=(x-2)^3+7\\(x-2)^3&=-7\\x-2&=-\sqrt[3]{7}\\x&=2-\sqrt[3]{7}\end{align*}$$
The inflection point is $(2,7)$. Sketch an increasing cubic through the intercepts, flattening at $(2,7)$.

spec.description: Increasing cubic with two-ended axes and curve arrows, no ticks or grid. Complete intercept coordinates include the missing source y-intercept label.
spec.mathematics: y=(x-2)^3+7; intercepts (0,-1) and (2-cuberoot(7),0); inflection (2,7). Plot coordinates are schematic viewing bounds, not prescribed axis ranges.

The inflection point is $(3,0)$. Sketch a decreasing cubic through $(0,27)$, flattening as it crosses the $x$-axis at $(3,0)$.

When $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=8(0)^3+12\\y&=12\end{align*}$$

The inflection point is $(0,12)$. Sketch an increasing cubic through the intercepts, flattening at $(0,12)$.

When $x\to\infty$, $y\to-\infty$.

Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-2(0-3)^3+8\\y&=54+8\\y&=62\end{align*}$$
Let $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-2(x-3)^3+8\\2(x-3)^3&=8\\(x-3)^3&=4\\x-3&=\sqrt[3]{4}\\x&=3+\sqrt[3]{4}\end{align*}$$
The inflection point is $(3,8)$. Sketch a decreasing cubic through the intercepts, flattening at $(3,8)$.

answer.short: $x$-intercept: $(3,0)$; $y$-intercept: $(0,-18)$. Increasing cubic with point of inflection $(1,-16)$.
answer.worked:
When $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(0-1)^3-16\\y&=-18\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,-18)$.

Let $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=2(x-1)^3-16\\16&=2(x-1)^3\\8&=(x-1)^3\\2&=x-1\\3&=x\end{align*}$$
The $x$-intercept is $(3,0)$. The point of inflection is $(1,-16)$. Sketch an increasing cubic through the intercepts, flattening at the point of inflection.

answer.short: $x$-intercept: $(-1-\sqrt[3]{5},0)$; $y$-intercept: $(0,-6)$. Decreasing cubic with point of inflection $(-1,-5)$.
answer.worked:
Behaviour: as $x\to\infty$, $y\to-\infty$.

Let $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=-(0+1)^3-5\\y&=-6\end{align*}$$
The $y$-intercept is $(0,-6)$.

Let $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-(x+1)^3-5\\(x+1)^3&=-5\\x+1&=-\sqrt[3]{5}\\x&=-1-\sqrt[3]{5}\end{align*}$$
The $x$-intercept is $(-1-\sqrt[3]{5},0)$.

The point of inflection is $(-1,-5)$. Sketch a decreasing cubic through the intercepts, flattening at the point of inflection.
